title: INTRAPRENEURSHIP
mv: And whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not to men.
mvp: “And whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not to men.” Colossians 3:23 (NKJV)
assignment: Mention five (5) challenges of being an intrapreneur (2x5=10 marks).

b.x: There are many possible situations where a potential entrepreneur does not get a chance to establish or fund his or her own business and is forced to work in an organisation. These people are referred to as ‘Intrapreneurs.’ Intrapreneurship refers to the practice of demonstrating entrepreneurial thinking within an existing organisation. It is taking initiative, solving problems, improving systems, and creating value where one serves, whether in the church, workplace, ministry, or community. Intrapreneurs do not wait for instructions; they use their God-given initiative and wisdom to make things happen (Colossians 3:23).

God expects His children to maximise the opportunities available to them. Like the servants in the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), intrapreneurs use what is in their hands to add value. They are not passive workers; rather, they take ownership, bring solutions, and improve results. Intrapreneurship thrives on excellence. Daniel excelled in Babylon because he had “an intrapreneurial spirit” (Daniel 6:3). This made him a problem-solver and positioned him for leadership. Believers should always seek better ways to improve processes, reduce waste, enhance quality, and think creatively to achieve results.

Intrapreneurs are not spectators; they are solution-drivers who anticipate needs and act intentionally. Joseph showed the intrapreneurial spirit of vision and initiative in Potiphar’s house and in prison (Genesis 39:1-6; 20-23). He saw problems ahead and designed solutions without being asked (Genesis 41:29-37). God blesses initiatives, especially when driven by wisdom and humility (1 Kings 3:28). Intrapreneurship must be built on integrity (Proverbs 22:1). Creativity and innovation cannot replace honesty, accountability, and loyalty; God promotes those who can be trusted (Luke 16:10).

i: Growth Mindset: Refuse mediocrity and embrace continuous improvement. Intrapreneurs constantly learn, research, practice new skills, and embrace change (1 Timothy 4:15).

Problem-Solving Skill: Every organisation has challenges. Instead of complaining, intrapreneurs prayerfully seek solutions. Through God’s wisdom (James 1:5), they propose strategies, design systems, and implement creative ideas for advancement.

Collaboration and Team Spirit: Intrapreneurship is not rebellion or acting independently; it is working with others to add value (Ecclesiastes 4:9). Effective intrapreneurs communicate well, seek feedback, respect leadership, and build unity.

Service to God: Christian Intrapreneurs must handle their work as a form of worship and recognise that their brilliance and creativity are a gift from God (1Corinthians 4:7; James 1:17). This mindset will help keep their motives pure and command God’s blessing.

b.x: Intrapreneurship empowers believers to be value-creators wherever God has placed them.
